The open risk is the Q4 guide against a single-source street Q4 of $93.5m and a reiterated 'FY broadly flat' that needs roughly $93m in Q4. Findings sum to +1.9. The scaled number is p_up 55 x abs 5.5 = +0.55, smaller because the bar is single-sourced and the guide can cut either way.

next_guide.basis: H1 2026 was $161.6m. A flat FY needs about $180m in H2, i.e. about $93m in Q4 if Q3 prints about $87m. Yalla's Q4 guides have been ranges like $78-85m, so a Q4 range with a midpoint in the high $80s is likely: FY stays 'broadly in line' at -1 to -2% while the Q4 guide sits below the single-source street $93.5m. The SLG title's Q4 major version and Turbo Match monetisation are the upside.

findings.finding: Yalla gave the identical Q3 guide ($78-85m) a year ago and printed $89.6m, 5.4% over the top. Q3 is seasonally its strongest quarter (Q3 2025 $89.6m vs Q2 2025 $84.6m, +5.9%), and Q2 2026 already beat its top at $82.6m. Applying last year's Q2-to-Q3 step gives about $87.5m, above the $85m top and about at the single-source street $87.2m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Quarters that beat the guide top: +4.12% (Q2 2026) and +1.0% (Q3 2025). Quarters inside the guide: -6.65% (Q1 2026) and -8.3% (Q4 2025). The stock punishes 'inside guide' more than it rewards 'above'.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the street $87.2m already sits above the guide top. What is not priced is a number at or above $88-90m, a repeat of last year's 5% over-delivery; if the market expected that, the stock would not trade at about net cash.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 guide and actual from the Q3 2025 release (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/36033942/yalla-group-limited-announces-unaudited-third-quarter-2025-financial-results); a different document from the Q2 2026 release.

findings.finding: Gulf non-oil activity recovered through Q3 despite the ongoing Iran war: the UAE PMI was 55.3 in both August and September (a 20-month high), and Saudi Arabia's rose from 53.8 to 55.3 with new orders at their fastest since February. Management said on 2026-08-17 that sequential MAU growth would resume in Q3. Together these point to paying users (10.9m in Q2 vs 11.2m) stabilising after the war-driven drop.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Paying-user declines blamed on 'geopolitical events' came with the -6.65% (Q1 2026) and -8.3% (Q4 2025) reactions; the Q2 rebound in flagship products came with +4.12%.
findings.why_not_priced: A business PMI is a proxy for spending on social apps, and the company has not confirmed the link. The stock fell 3.4% over 20 days rather than rising, so the market has not credited a regional recovery.
findings.independence: Proxy. The management MAU remark is on the Q2 call transcript (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262114446-tradingkey); the war is still described as ongoing (Hormuz attacks).

findings.finding: Management reiterated on 2026-08-17 that FY2026 revenue would be 'broadly in line' with FY2025 ($341.9m). With H1 at $161.6m, that needs about $180m in H2, roughly $93m in Q4 if Q3 prints about $87m. That matches the single-source street Q4 of $93.5m, while Yalla's Q4 guides have historically been ranges like $78-85m. A Q4 guide midpoint in the high $80s would leave FY at about -1 to -2% and below the street's Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: beat top by 5% but guided Q4 at $78-85m, below the Q3 actual, and the stock only rose +1.0%. Q4 2025 print with the first FY-flat guide: -8.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market believed the FY-flat guide and the $93.5m street Q4, the stock would not sit about at net cash. So a soft Q4 guide is partly priced, which is why this is sized small; a strong Q4 guide (SLG major version, Turbo Match monetisation) is the upside case.
findings.independence: The street Q4 is one Benzinga snippet (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/YALA/earnings-forecasts); FY2025 $341.9m and Q4 2025 guide history are from the Q4 2025 release (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/650416/yalla-group-limited-announces-unaudited-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial-results).

findings.why_not_priced: It is the price. The point is asymmetry: an ordinary print has little left to disappoint, and the stock has drifted -3.4% into the print rather than run up.

findings.finding: The new $150m repurchase programme (from 2026-03-09) and the active buyback ($18.0m in Q2, $27.6m in H1 across both programmes, 12.7m shares cancelled by 2026-08-14) will show a Q3 repurchase figure in the release. The programme is a support for the price after the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buybacks have been disclosed every quarter; I found no isolated reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The programme is known; Q3 execution and any step-up are not. With 339k ADS a day of volume, an $18m-a-quarter buyer is a meaningful share of turnover.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 1 for the H1 figures; the share-cancellation figure is from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262114446-tradingkey).

findings.finding: Management guided H2 costs and expenses to be 'broadly similar to the first half'. Q2 operating income was $19.4m on $82.6m (23.5%, vs 36% a year earlier) after selling and marketing doubled to $17.8m. A seasonally higher Q3 revenue on flat costs should lift operating margin quarter on quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: I have no isolated margin-surprise reaction; Q2 rose +4.12% despite the margin drop.
findings.why_not_priced: I found no EPS consensus. Management also flagged it 'may continue to increase user acquisition investment', so the margin read is two-sided and sized small.
findings.independence: The cost lines are from the Q2 release (technode), a different document from the call.
